transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivers (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions), Laura Chen (Head of ML, Nimbus), Raj Patel (CTO), Samir Gupta (Platform Eng), Ellen Ortiz (Security)

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood structured output / JSON mode and function/tool-calling (demo of console + API + Optimize guardrails). Customer wants deterministic structured outputs for downstream processing (payments reconciliation, KYC flagging) and assurances on schema enforcement and fallbacks.

Topics: structured output, function calling/tool calling, JSON mode, schemas, guardrails, Console walkthrough, Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization), security (KMS, audit logs), next steps for POC

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll be running today, um ethan's gonna do the deep demo parts.
[00:09] Laura Chen: hi maya, thanks, excited. we basically want to see structured output JSON and the function calling flow — our downstream pipelines break on inconsistent keys so this is top priority.
[00:18] Maya Patel: totally makes sense. quick intro, redwood provides hosted + dedicated + private, but for this session we'll focus on the API + console tool where you can toggle JSON mode and function-calling guardrails, and also a couple bits in Optimize that give quantization/ batching recs.
[00:33] Ethan Rivers: yeah i'll share my screen in a sec, we'll demo the console first then run an API call live. note: sometimes the console auto-suggest labels redwood-verify as redwood-rectify in the transcript, sorry if i mis-say product names.
[00:46] Raj Patel: quick question on deployment modes — we are evaluating both hosted and private for data residency; which of those supports schema locking?
[00:53] Jordan Lee: schema locking is an API/ runtime feature, works in hosted and dedicated; for private we ship the same control plane features when you run the private control plane with KMS integration. there are small ops differences but the JSON guarded outputs are available across modes.
[01:06] Samir Gupta: cool. can you show an example where the model returns nested arrays and we validate/normalize them? that's been a pain.
[01:13] Ethan Rivers: yes, so i'll open the console — ok screen share up — this is the console run tab, see 'structured output' toggle, 'schema' area. i'll paste a JSON schema for a payments reconciliation payload.
[01:30] Ethan Rivers: (typing) the schema enforces fields: transaction_id string, amount number in cents, currency enum [USD, EUR], merchant object with id and category, flags array of enums. i'll enable "strict mode" which enforces types and will either return an error or a best-effort repair depending on policy.
[01:50] Laura Chen: when it repairs — is there an audit trail showing what was changed? we need provenance.
[01:56] Ethan Rivers: yes, every repair or schema deviation is logged in the response metadata and in the Console trace; you can toggle "log diffs" and it'll include before/after snippets. those logs are retained per your retention policy and can be exported to S3 or forwarded to your SIEM.
[02:12] Ellen Ortiz: retention and encryption — does the hosted option let us use our KMS?
[02:18] Jordan Lee: hosted supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration and HSM for enterprise; private gets your own key material. we'll share the security whitepaper after this call.
[02:27] Raj Patel: ok back to function calling — how does tool calling differ from 'structured output mode'?
[02:33] Ethan Rivers: good question. structured output (JSON mode) is enforcing a schema for the model's text output. function/tool calling is about the model returning an invocation for a callable action — e.g., call the reconciliation service with the structured payload. we support both: the model can emit a guarded JSON that also contains a function call envelope. we demonstrated that in our sample where the model returns {"name":"reconcile_tx","args":{...}}.
[02:56] Laura Chen: will that ever execute automatically? security team wants explicit approval.
[03:01] Maya Patel: by default in the Console function calls are dry-run; to execute you have to opt-in at the route level. we also support RBAC and execution policies (can only run from certain routes or IP ranges).
[03:13] Samir Gupta: latency concerns — if we do validation and repair what is typical added latency?
[03:19] Ethan Rivers: validation is lightweight, sub-10ms normally. repair can be rule-based or model-assisted; the latter adds variable time — we show estimated added latency in the Console per-request. with dedicated capacity we've seen median end-to-end under 150ms for structured outputs on 512-token jobs.
[03:37] Raj Patel: and costs? model-assisted repair sounds expensive.
[03:41] Ethan Rivers: Optimize will recommend whether to move repairs to a secondary lightweight model or to local rule engine. we give unit cost estimates in Optimize — you can see token delta and CPU/GPU usage; often splitting repair to a small deterministic service cuts costs by 60-80%.
[03:58] Laura Chen: demo the API call please, with a schema and function call.
[04:02] Ethan Rivers: switching to API example — here's a curl. (reads) POST /v1/generate with body {"mode":"json","schema":<schema>, "function_call": {"name":"reconcile_tx"}, "input":"process these 3 transactions"} — the response includes output, json, and function_call fields.
[04:25] [04:25] Ethan Rivers: i'll paste the raw response — notice the model returned a slightly malformed amount for one tx (7,500 -> "75.00" with decimal). with strict policy set to 'error' the response would have errored; with 'repair' it returned corrected integer cents and added a repair_log.
[04:44] Laura Chen: perfect, we need both behaviors depending on route. for our settlement pipeline it's error-fail, for analytics it's repair.
[04:52] Maya Patel: you can set per-route policies in the console and pin them to model versions. we also support canaries so you can try repair=false on a subset and monitor regressions.
[05:05] Raj Patel: any examples of schema drift detection? we currently run nightly checks but it'd be great to have built-in alerts.
[05:11] Ethan Rivers: Optimize has a schema-regression monitor — it runs prompt/eval sets and flags distributional drift, mismatched enums, and increased repair rates. alerts can post to Slack or to the Console signals view.
[05:25] Samir Gupta: on the function calling side — what happens if the model suggests calling an unexpected function name or an external URL?
[05:32] Jordan Lee: all callable functions are whitelisted by name and signature at route config; any unknown function is rejected. you can also set a domain allowlist for webhooks.
[05:41] Ellen Ortiz: audit logs for function execution? we need immutable logs for SOC 2.
[05:46] Ethan Rivers: yes, every invocation is recorded with request/response metadata, user ID, route, and execution decision (executed/blocked/dry-run). immutable retention and export supported.
[05:57] Laura Chen: can you demo a guardrail where the model is not allowed to hallucinate arbitrary merchant categories — basically strict enums?
[06:03] Ethan Rivers: sure — the schema here pins merchant.category to an enum list. i'll force the model to invent a nonsense category. (types) the model initially replied "astral_services" but the validator replaced it with 'misc' and added a repair note. here's the trace.
[06:24] [06:24] Ethan Rivers: note, transcription: occasionally redwood console is verbalized as 'redwood con' in auto transcripts — ignore small name swaps.
[06:30] Raj Patel: fine. what's the recommended model sizing for heavy throughput? we do 10k req/s spikes.
[06:36] Ethan Rivers: for 10k req/s you want dedicated pools with autoscale and batching; Optimize suggests pool sizes and batching windows. model distillation/quantization also helps — we have q4_0/q5 profiles that reduce GPU memory and cost, Optimize will recommend quantization profile per model+workload.
[06:55] Laura Chen: are quantized models still compatible with structured output guarantees? we've seen quality drops.
[07:01] Ethan Rivers: good point — Optimize includes evals so you'll see regression alerts on your golden prompt set. for mission-critical pipelines we'd recommend A/Bing between full-precision and quantized models with canary rollout.
[07:14] Samir Gupta: any specific SDK examples for function calling? we use python in our platform.
[07:19] Ethan Rivers: yes, in the SDK you call client.generate(..., mode='json', schema=..., functions=[...]). there's a function-calling helper that validates args client-side before sending and can optionally short-circuit if local rules fail. i'll drop code snippets in the follow-up.
[07:33] Laura Chen: please include a sample where client validates enums locally to reduce failed calls.
[07:38] Ethan Rivers: noted.
[07:40] Raj Patel: security — pen tests? do you have certs?
[07:44] Jordan Lee: we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001, and provide pen test summaries under NDA. we can provide a SOC package and security questionnaire.
[07:55] Ellen Ortiz: okay please send the security pack and KMS integration docs.
[07:59] Maya Patel: will do.
[08:02] Laura Chen: one more question — can we have the model return structured output plus a human readable summary in the same response? some teams prefer both.
[08:09] Ethan Rivers: yes, the response supports multiple channels: text, json, and function_call. you can ask for a 'summary' field in the schema or request the textual summary in the plain output. the Console shows both side-by-side.
[08:21] Samir Gupta: miscellaneous meta — how do you surface token-level cost attribution?
[08:26] Jordan Lee: Console and the API return token breakdowns; Optimize will attribute cost per route/model and give recommendations to reduce unit cost.
[08:36] Laura Chen: ok we're near time, this was helpful. can you recap next steps?
[08:41] Maya Patel: recap: we'll send sandbox creds + demo recording + pricing; ethan to send schema examples, SDK snippets, and guardrail best practices; nimbus to run bench and share sample payloads; security to get SOC docs and KMS guide. schedule follow-up poc scoping on 2025-07-01.
[08:59] Raj Patel: thanks all.
[09:02] Maya Patel: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts Shared: Console demo recording link: https://redwood.example.com/demo-recordings/rec-20250625, Sandbox invite: invite link (sent via email), Security pack (link to share under NDA), Schema examples (will attach in follow-up).
